claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1Q.

claims.claim: The Bmp5-expressing neuromasts in the main body line at stage 45 are secondary neuromasts deposited by the later-migrating primII, which are offset slightly dorsally to those deposited earlier by primI.
claims.source: The Bmp5-expressing neuromasts in the main body line are secondary neuromasts deposited by the later-migrating primII, which are offset slightly dorsally to those deposited earlier by primI, which are Bmp5-negative (compare with Cacna1d expression in Figure 1R; examples of primII-deposited neuromasts are highlighted).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1Q and R.

claims.claim: Bmp5 is expressed early within ampullary organ primordia and maintained in mature ampullary organs at least through to the onset of independent feeding at stage 45 in sterlet.
claims.source: Overall, these results suggest that Bmp5 is expressed early within ampullary organ primordia and maintained in mature ampullary organs at least through to the onset of independent feeding at stage 45.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Bmp5 is only expressed in mature neuromasts in sterlet, after the onset of hair cell differentiation, and then only transiently.
claims.source: In contrast, Bmp5 only seems to be expressed in mature neuromasts, after the onset of hair cell differentiation, and then only transiently.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: At stage 30, faint pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the region of the anteroventral lateral line primordium in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 30 (the earliest stage examined), faint pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the region of the anteroventral lateral line primordium (Figure 2A and B; compare with Sox2 immunoreactivity at stage 32 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B; Sox2 is expressed in lateral line primordia and maintained in supporting cells; Hernández et al., 2007; Modrell et al., 2017a; Minařík et al., 2024a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claims.claim: Sox2 is expressed in lateral line primordia and maintained in supporting cells.
claims.source: At stage 30 (the earliest stage examined), faint pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the region of the anteroventral lateral line primordium (Figure 2A and B; compare with Sox2 immunoreactivity at stage 32 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B; Sox2 is expressed in lateral line primordia and maintained in supporting cells; Hernández et al., 2007; Modrell et al., 2017a; Minařík et al., 2024a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claims.claim: By stage 34, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia, with a ring pattern around developing neuromast primordia in the otic/anterodorsal and anteroventral primordia in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 34, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia, with a ring pattern around developing neuromast primordia in the otic/anterodorsal and anteroventral primordia (Figure 2C and D; compare with stage 35 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: The first Cacna1d-positive differentiated hair cells are seen in the otic/anterodorsal and anteroventral primordia region at stage 35 in sterlet.
claims.source: (The first Cacna1d-positive differentiated hair cells are seen in this region at stage 35; Minařík et al., 2024a.)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: At stage 36, weak pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was still seen around developing neuromasts in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 36 (Figure 2E and F), weak pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was still seen around developing neuromasts (compare with stage 37 Cacna1d expression in Figure 1C and D; stage 37 Sox2 immunoreactivity in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F), but we were intrigued to see more prominent immunoreactivity in a filamentous pattern that seemed most likely to correspond to lateral line nerves (Figure 2E and F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claims.claim: At stage 36, more prominent pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in a filamentous pattern that seemed most likely to correspond to lateral line nerves in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 36 (Figure 2E and F), weak pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was still seen around developing neuromasts (compare with stage 37 Cacna1d expression in Figure 1C and D; stage 37 Sox2 immunoreactivity in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F), but we were intrigued to see more prominent immunoreactivity in a filamentous pattern that seemed most likely to correspond to lateral line nerves (Figure 2E and F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E and F, and is an inference about the identity of the labeled structures.

claims.claim: The filamentous pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity continued at stages 38 and 40 in sterlet.
claims.source: This pattern continued at stages 38 and 40 (Figure 2G–J); indeed pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactive collaterals seemed to be developing from the infraorbital nerve between stages 38 and 40 (Figure 2G–J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2G-J.

claims.claim: pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactive collaterals seemed to be developing from the infraorbital nerve between stages 38 and 40 in sterlet.
claims.source: This pattern continued at stages 38 and 40 (Figure 2G–J); indeed pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactive collaterals seemed to be developing from the infraorbital nerve between stages 38 and 40 (Figure 2G–J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2G-J, and is an inference about the developmental process.

claims.claim: At stage 40, diffuse pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was also seen in regions flanking the nerves where ampullary organ primordia are forming in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 40, diffuse immunoreactivity was also seen in regions flanking the nerves where ampullary organ primordia are forming (Figure 2I and J; compare with stage 40 Bmp5 expression in Figure 1E and F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2I and J.

claims.claim: Strong pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in the barbel primordia, around the nares and mouth, in gill filaments, and between stages 36 and 40 in a patch between the barbels and the otic vesicle that likely represents a muscle, the m. protractor hyomandibulae, in sterlet.
claims.source: (Strong pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was also seen in the barbel primordia, around the nares and mouth, in gill filaments, and between stages 36 and 40 in a patch between the barbels and the otic vesicle that likely represents a muscle, the m. protractor hyomandibulae; Warth et al., 2018.)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2, and the identification of the muscle is supported by a citation.

claims.claim: By stage 42, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was visible in ampullary organs and much less prominent in lateral line nerves in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 42, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was visible in ampullary organs and much less prominent in lateral line nerves (Figure 2K and L; compare with stage 42 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I and J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2K and L.

claims.claim: At stages 43 and 45, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was more clearly visible in neuromasts as well as ampullary organs, in all cases at the periphery rather than centre of each organ in sterlet.
claims.source: At stages 43 and 45, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was more clearly visible in neuromasts as well as ampullary organs, in all cases at the periphery rather than centre of each organ (Figure 2M–P; compare with the hair cell/electroreceptor marker Cacna1d at stage 42 in Figure 1K and L and at stage 45 in Figure 1O and P, and the supporting cell marker Sox2 at stages 42 and 45 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I–L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2M-P.

claims.claim: The peripheral pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity suggests that Bmp signalling is active in supporting cells rather than receptor cells in sterlet.
claims.source: This peripheral pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity suggests that Bmp signalling is active in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the immunohistochemistry data and the known locations of supporting cells versus receptor cells.

claims.claim: At stages 43 and 45, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity on the head seemed to be particularly strong in the supraorbital and infraorbital neuromast lines in sterlet.
claims.source: Also at stages 43 and 45, we noted that pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity on the head seemed to be particularly strong in the supraorbital and infraorbital neuromast lines (compare with Sox2 expression at stages 42 and 45 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I–L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2M-P.

claims.claim: At stage 39, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in primI and a diffuse but somewhat continuous line trailing behind it, as well as in primII, which is located much further rostrally and a little dorsal to the main line in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 39, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in primI and a diffuse but somewhat continuous line trailing behind it, as well as in primII, which is located much further rostrally and a little dorsal to the main line (Figure 2Q; compare with Sox2 expression in Figure 2R).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2Q.

claims.claim: At stage 45, strong pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in primII and primD, and more weakly along the path taken by primII, with increased intensity at the periphery of the primII-deposited neuromasts in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 45, strong pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen in primII and primD, and more weakly along the path taken by primII, with increased intensity at the periphery of the primII-deposited neuromasts (Figure 2S; compare with Sox2 expression in all neuromasts in Figure 2T and with Bmp5 expression in primII-deposited neuromasts in Figure 1Q).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2S.

claims.claim: Bmp signalling is active throughout lateral line development in the sterlet, including lateral line organ primordia and even lateral line nerves, and later at the periphery (rather than the centre) of maturing ampullary organs and neuromasts.
claims.source: Overall, these data suggest that Bmp signalling is active throughout lateral line development in the sterlet, including lateral line organ primordia and even lateral line nerves, and later at the periphery (rather than the centre) of maturing ampullary organs and neuromasts, suggesting activity in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Bmp signalling activity at the periphery of maturing ampullary organs and neuromasts suggests activity in supporting cells rather than receptor cells in sterlet.
claims.source: Overall, these data suggest that Bmp signalling is active throughout lateral line development in the sterlet, including lateral line organ primordia and even lateral line nerves, and later at the periphery (rather than the centre) of maturing ampullary organs and neuromasts, suggesting activity in supporting cells rather than receptor cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the immunohistochemistry data and the known locations of supporting cells versus receptor cells.

claims.claim: Bmp5 was the only gene encoding a Bmp ligand or receptor in the late-larval paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene-set.
claims.source: Bmp5 was the only gene encoding a Bmp ligand or receptor in the late-larval paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene-set (Modrell et al., 2017a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data from a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: The timecourse and pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity in the developing sterlet lateral line system was more extensive than Bmp5 expression, suggesting other Bmp ligands must be expressed.
claims.source: However, the timecourse and pattern of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity in the developing sterlet lateral line system was more extensive than Bmp5 expression (compare Figure 1 and Figure 2), suggesting other Bmp ligands must be expressed that were not enriched in the transcriptome of late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue (Modrell et al., 2017a).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the Bmp5 expression data (Figure 1) with the pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity data (Figure 2).

claims.claim: Bmp4 expression was not evident in the developing sterlet lateral line at stage 37 or stage 38.
claims.source: Bmp4 expression was not evident in the developing sterlet lateral line at stage 37 or stage 38 (Figure 3A–D); the very faint expression in two widely spaced dorsal patches at stage 38 may be sensory patches in the otic vesicle (Figure 3C and D), or may represent early-forming neuromast primordia in the otic and supratemporal lines (see Gibbs and Northcutt, 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claims.claim: The very faint Bmp4 expression in two widely spaced dorsal patches at stage 38 may be sensory patches in the otic vesicle, or may represent early-forming neuromast primordia in the otic and supratemporal lines in sterlet.
claims.source: Bmp4 expression was not evident in the developing sterlet lateral line at stage 37 or stage 38 (Figure 3A–D); the very faint expression in two widely spaced dorsal patches at stage 38 may be sensory patches in the otic vesicle (Figure 3C and D), or may represent early-forming neuromast primordia in the otic and supratemporal lines (see Gibbs and Northcutt, 2004).
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the identity of the Bmp4-expressing structures, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Stronger Bmp4 expression was seen in fin, barbel and gill filament primordia, and around the nares at stages 37 and 38 in sterlet.
claims.source: Stronger expression was also seen in fin, barbel and gill filament primordia, and around the nares (Figure 3A–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claims.claim: By stage 40, diffuse Bmp4 expression was observed in neuromast regions and fields of ampullary organ primordia on the head in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 40, diffuse Bmp4 expression was observed in neuromast regions and fields of ampullary organ primordia on the head (Figure 3E and F; compare with Bmp5 and Cacna1d expression in Figure 1E–H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: At stage 40, stronger Bmp4 expression was seen on the trunk in primI, with much weaker expression in the most recently deposited neuromasts near to the primordium, plus a spot that most likely represents primII in sterlet.
claims.source: Stronger expression was also seen on the trunk in primI, with much weaker expression in the most recently deposited neuromasts near to the primordium, plus a spot that most likely represents primII (Figure 3G; compare with stage 40 Sox2 expression on the trunk in Figure 2—figure supplement 1N).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3G, and the identification of primII is an inference.

claims.claim: At stage 42, Bmp4 expression in lateral line regions on the head was almost gone, with only faint expression remaining in the dorsal infraorbital ampullary organ field, just below the eye in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 42, Bmp4 expression in lateral line regions on the head was almost gone, with only faint expression remaining in the dorsal infraorbital ampullary organ field, just below the eye (Figure 3H and I).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claims.claim: At stage 42, strong Bmp4 expression was seen in primII and primD on the trunk in sterlet.
claims.source: However, strong expression was seen in primII and primD on the trunk (Figure 3J; compare with stage 42 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1O).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3J.

claims.claim: By stage 45, Bmp4 was no longer expressed in lateral line regions on the head, although expression remained in the barbels and gills in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 45, Bmp4 was no longer expressed in lateral line regions on the head, although expression remained in the barbels and gills (Figure 3K–L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3K-L.

claims.claim: At stage 45, the migrating lateral line primordia on the trunk still expressed Bmp4 in sterlet.
claims.source: As at stages 40 and 42, the migrating lateral line primordia on the trunk still expressed Bmp4 at stage 45 (Figure 3M; compare with stage 45 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1P).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3M.

claims.claim: Bmp4 plays a more transient role than Bmp5 in lateral line organ development in sterlet.
claims.source: These data suggest that Bmp4 plays a more transient role than Bmp5 in lateral line organ development.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the Bmp4 expression data (Figure 3) with the Bmp5 expression data (Figure 1).

claims.claim: An as-yet unidentified Bmp ligand gene is most likely expressed in lateral line primordia before either Bmp5 or Bmp4 in sterlet.
claims.source: Furthermore, most likely an as-yet unidentified Bmp ligand gene is expressed in lateral line primordia before either Bmp5 or Bmp4, given that pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was detectable in lateral line primordia at stage 34 (Figure 2C and D).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity data (Figure 2C and D) and the absence of Bmp5 and Bmp4 expression at that stage.

claims.claim: Acvr2a encodes ActRIIA (activin A receptor type 2 A), a type II Bmp receptor that promiscuously binds multiple ligands including Bmp5 and Bmp4.
claims.source: The only Bmp receptor gene we examined was Acvr2a, encoding ActRIIA (activin A receptor type 2 A), a type II Bmp receptor that promiscuously binds multiple ligands including Bmp5 and Bmp4 (Yadin et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claims.claim: Acvr2a was not expressed at stage 37 in sterlet, so other receptors must be involved in mediating Bmp signalling in lateral line primordia at this and earlier stages.
claims.source: Acvr2a was not expressed at stage 37 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), so other receptors must be involved in mediating Bmp signalling in lateral line primordia at this and earlier stages (see, for example, pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity at stage 34 and stage 36; Figure 2C–F).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of Acvr2a expression at stage 37 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) and the presence of pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity at earlier stages (Figure 2C-F).

claims.claim: By stage 38, Acvr2a expression was detectable in developing neuromast regions in sterlet, although background levels were high.
claims.source: By stage 38, although background levels were high, Acvr2a expression was detectable in developing neuromast regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claims.claim: By stage 40, Acvr2a was expressed at the periphery of ampullary organ primordia and neuromasts on the head in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 40, Acvr2a was expressed at the periphery of ampullary organ primordia and neuromasts on the head (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F; compare with stage 40 Bmp5 and Cacna1d expression in Figure 1E–H, and with stage 39 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claims.claim: At stage 40, Acvr2a was expressed in primI and a trailing line of cells behind it, plus a spot most likely representing primII in sterlet.
claims.source: Also at stage 40, Acvr2a was expressed in primI and a trailing line of cells behind it, plus a spot most likely representing primII (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, and the identification of primII is an inference.

claims.claim: At stage 42, Acvr2a expression persisted in both the head and trunk, with expression now also seen in primD and in the rostral trunk neuromasts deposited by primII in sterlet.
claims.source: This pattern persisted in both the head and trunk at stage 42, with expression now also seen primD and in the rostral trunk neuromasts deposited by primII (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-J.

claims.claim: By stage 45, Acvr2a expression appeared to be fading on the head, with only faint expression at the periphery of ampullary organs in a few areas in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 45, Acvr2a expression appeared to be fading on the head, with only faint expression at the periphery of ampullary organs in a few areas (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K and L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K and L.

claims.claim: At stage 45, Acvr2a expression continued in the trunk neuromast lines in sterlet.
claims.source: However, expression continued in the trunk neuromast lines (Figure 3—figure supplement 1M).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1M.

claims.claim: The Acvr2a expression pattern does not fully complement either Bmp5 or Bmp4 expression, or pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity, suggesting other type II receptor(s), as well as type I receptors, must be involved in sterlet.
claims.source: Overall, the Acvr2a expression pattern does not fully complement either Bmp5 or Bmp4 expression (compare with Figure 1 and Figure 3, respectively), or pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity (Figure 2). Hence, other type II receptor(s), as well of course as type I receptors, must be involved.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the Acvr2a expression data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) with the Bmp5 expression data (Figure 1), Bmp4 expression data (Figure 3), and pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity data (Figure 2).

claims.claim: Three genes encoding secreted Bmp inhibitors were present in the late-larval paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene-set: Sostdc1, Apcdd1 and Vwc2.
claims.source: Three genes encoding secreted Bmp inhibitors were present in the late-larval paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene-set (Modrell et al., 2017a): Sostdc1, Apcdd1 and Vwc2.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data from a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: Vwc2 was 4.5-fold lateral line-enriched in the late-larval paddlefish lateral line-enriched gene-set.
claims.source: Vwc2 was 4.5-fold lateral line-enriched (Modrell et al., 2017a), but ISH for this gene in sterlet was unsuccessful so it is not considered further.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data from a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: Sostdc1 (sclerostin domain-containing 1; also known as Wise, Ectodin) is a secreted antagonist of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways.
claims.source: Sostdc1 (sclerostin domain-containing 1; also known as Wise, Ectodin) is a secreted antagonist of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways (Tong et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claims.claim: Sostdc1 was 4.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue.
claims.source: Sostdc1 was 4.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue (Modrell et al., 2017a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data from a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: From stage 36 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in lines of differentiated neuromasts (and in gill filament primordia) on the head in sterlet.
claims.source: From stage 36 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in lines of differentiated neuromasts (and in gill filament primordia) on the head, and from stage 40 onwards, in the migrating primordia and neuromasts on the trunk (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–M; compare with Cacna1d expression in Figure 1 and Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-P).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-M.

claims.claim: From stage 40 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in the migrating primordia and neuromasts on the trunk in sterlet.
claims.source: From stage 36 onwards, Sostdc1 expression was seen in lines of differentiated neuromasts (and in gill filament primordia) on the head, and from stage 40 onwards, in the migrating primordia and neuromasts on the trunk (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–M; compare with Cacna1d expression in Figure 1 and Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-P).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-M.

claims.claim: At stage 42, Sostdc1 expression was also detected in ampullary organs in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 42, Sostdc1 expression was also detected in ampullary organs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H and I), but this had already disappeared by stage 45 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K and L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2H and I.

claims.claim: Sostdc1 expression in ampullary organs had already disappeared by stage 45 in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 42, Sostdc1 expression was also detected in ampullary organs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H and I), but this had already disappeared by stage 45 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K and L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2K and L.

claims.claim: Sostdc1 plays a persistent role within neuromasts in sterlet.

claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Sostdc1 expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Any function of Sostdc1 in ampullary organ development is likely to be transient in sterlet.
claims.source: These data suggest Sostdc1 plays a persistent role within neuromasts, but any function in ampullary organ development is likely to be transient.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Sostdc1 expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Apcdd1 (adenomatosis polyposis coli down-regulated 1) is a secreted inhibitor of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways.
claims.source: Apcdd1 (adenomatosis polyposis coli down-regulated 1) is also a secreted inhibitor of both the Bmp and Wnt pathways (Vonica et al., 2020).

claims.claim: Apcdd1 was 2.2-fold enriched in late-larval paddlefish operculum versus fin tissue.

claims.claim: At stage 36, there was some Apcdd1 expression in the region of the preopercular neuromast line, as well as outside the lateral line system: at the edge of the operculum, near the future barbel region and around the mouth in sterlet.
claims.source: However, there was some Apcdd1 expression in the region of the preopercular neuromast line, as well as outside the lateral line system: at the edge of the operculum, near the future barbel region and around the mouth (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B.

claims.claim: At stage 38, more diffuse Apcdd1 expression was seen in broader regions in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 38, more diffuse Apcdd1 expression was seen in broader regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D.

claims.claim: By stage 40, Apcdd1 expression was visible around ampullary organ primordia and some neuromasts on the head in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 40, expression was visible around ampullary organ primordia and some neuromasts on the head (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F), as well as primI and primII on the trunk and a relatively short line of trailing cells behind primI (Figure 3—figure supplement 3G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F.

claims.claim: At stage 40, Apcdd1 expression was seen in primI and primII on the trunk and a relatively short line of trailing cells behind primI in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 40, expression was visible around ampullary organ primordia and some neuromasts on the head (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F), as well as primI and primII on the trunk and a relatively short line of trailing cells behind primI (Figure 3—figure supplement 3G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3G.

claims.claim: By stage 42, Apcdd1 expression on the head had largely resolved to the periphery of ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 42, Apcdd1 expression on the head had largely resolved to the periphery of ampullary organs and neuromasts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3H and I; compare with stage 42 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I and J) and continued in the migrating primordia on the trunk and the short line of trailing cells behind primI (Figure 3—figure supplement 3J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3H and I.

claims.claim: At stage 42, Apcdd1 expression continued in the migrating primordia on the trunk and the short line of trailing cells behind primI in sterlet.
claims.source: By stage 42, Apcdd1 expression on the head had largely resolved to the periphery of ampullary organs and neuromasts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3H and I; compare with stage 42 Sox2 expression in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I and J) and continued in the migrating primordia on the trunk and the short line of trailing cells behind primI (Figure 3—figure supplement 3J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3J.

claims.claim: At stage 45, Apcdd1 expression pattern largely persisted, although it seemed to be fading in the ventral infraorbital field in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 45, this expression pattern largely persisted, although it seemed to be fading in the ventral infraorbital field (Figure 3—figure supplement 3K and L) and faint expression was also now seen along the main body line, potentially at the periphery of trunk neuromasts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3M; compare with stage 45 Sox2 expression on the trunk in Figure 2—figure supplement 1P).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3K and L.

claims.claim: At stage 45, faint Apcdd1 expression was also seen along the main body line, potentially at the periphery of trunk neuromasts in sterlet.
claims.source: At stage 45, this expression pattern largely persisted, although it seemed to be fading in the ventral infraorbital field (Figure 3—figure supplement 3K and L) and faint expression was also now seen along the main body line, potentially at the periphery of trunk neuromasts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3M; compare with stage 45 Sox2 expression on the trunk in Figure 2—figure supplement 1P).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3M, and the location is inferred by comparison with Sox2 expression.

claims.claim: The early, broad expression of Apcdd1 within ampullary organ fields and seemingly very late upregulation in neuromasts suggests that Apcdd1 may be more important for ampullary organ development in sterlet.
claims.source: These data, especially the early, broad expression within ampullary organ fields and seemingly very late upregulation in neuromasts, suggest that Apcdd1 may be more important for ampullary organ development.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Apcdd1 expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The pattern of Sostdc1 expression suggests its role may be more prominent during neuromast development in sterlet.
claims.source: In contrast, the pattern of Sostdc1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) suggests its role may be more prominent during neuromast development.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Sostdc1 expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Bmp5 was chosen as a target for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos owing to its earlier expression in ampullary organ primordia.
claims.source: Having established that the Bmp signalling pathway is active throughout lateral line organ development and that genes encoding two Bmp ligands, a type II receptor and two secreted dual Bmp/Wnt antagonists are expressed, we wanted to explore the role of Bmp signalling in lateral line development. Bmp5 was chosen as a target for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos owing to its earlier expression in ampullary organ primordia.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the rationale for the experimental design.

claims.claim: The sterlet genome has retained a high level of tetraploidy, including around 70% of ohnologs.
claims.source: Analysis of this genome showed that, rather than being functionally diploid as previously thought (from microsatellite data; Ludwig et al., 2001), the sterlet genome has retained a high level of tetraploidy, including around 70% of ohnologs (i.e., gene paralogs resulting from the independent whole-genome duplication in the sterlet lineage) (Du et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claims.claim: Both Bmp5 ohnologs have been retained in the sterlet genome, on chromosomes 5 and 6, with 88.87% nucleotide identity in the coding sequence (and 95.60% amino acid identity).
claims.source: Searching the reference genome (Vertebrate Genomes Project NCBI RefSeq assembly GCF_902713425.1) for Bmp5 showed that both Bmp5 ohnologs have been retained, on chromosomes 5 and 6, with 88.87% nucleotide identity in the coding sequence (and 95.60% amino acid identity).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome.

claims.claim: All of the Bmp5 sgRNAs fully match the ohnolog on chromosome 6.
claims.source: All of our Bmp5 sgRNAs fully match the ohnolog on chromosome 6.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome.

claims.claim: Bmp5 sgRNAs 2 and 4 each have a single-base mismatch with the chromosome 5 ohnolog, respectively, in positions 7 and 4 of the target sequence (PAM-distal), which should be tolerated.
claims.source: Relative to the ohnolog on chromosome 5, sgRNAs 2 and 4 (Table 1; Figure 4A) each have a single-base mismatch, respectively, in positions 7 and 4 of the target sequence (PAM-distal), which should be tolerated (Guo et al., 2014; Rabinowitz and Offen, 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome and citations to established literature about sgRNA tolerance of mismatches.

claims.claim: Bmp5 sgRNA 1 has two mismatched bases (at positions 3 and 12 of the target sequence) with the chromosome 5 ohnolog.
claims.source: However, our sgRNA 1 (Table 1; Figure 4A) has two mismatched bases (at positions 3 and 12 of the target sequence) and sgRNA 3 (Table 1; Figure 4A) has a single-base mismatch at position 20, adjacent to the PAM.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome.

claims.claim: Bmp5 sgRNA 3 has a single-base mismatch at position 20, adjacent to the PAM, with the chromosome 5 ohnolog.
claims.source: However, our sgRNA 1 (Table 1; Figure 4A) has two mismatched bases (at positions 3 and 12 of the target sequence) and sgRNA 3 (Table 1; Figure 4A) has a single-base mismatch at position 20, adjacent to the PAM.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome.

claims.claim: All sgRNA mixtures are expected to have targeted both Bmp5 ohnologs, given that all combinations of injected sgRNAs contained either sgRNA 2 or sgRNA 4.
claims.source: Therefore, although we expect all our sgRNAs to target the chromosome 6 ohnolog, it is possible that only sgRNAs 2 and 4 successfully target the chromosome 5 ohnolog (Guo et al., 2014; Rabinowitz and Offen, 2021). Nevertheless, given that all combinations of injected sgRNAs contained either sgRNA 2 or sgRNA 4 (Table 1; Supplementary file 1) we expect all mixtures to have targeted both Bmp5 ohnologs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the sgRNA design and the known tolerance of mismatches.

claims.claim: Relative to Tyr crispants (n=0/24), a mosaic reduction in Cacna1d expression in ampullary organ fields was observed in 46% of Bmp5 crispants (n=53/116).
claims.source: Ampullary organ numbers in different fields vary considerably across individual larvae even in wild-types, but relative to Tyr crispants (n=0/24; Figure 4A and B; Supplementary file 1), we observed a mosaic reduction in Cacna1d expression in ampullary organ fields in 46% of Bmp5 crispants (n=53/116; Figure 4C–F; Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4 and counting data in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: The efficacy of different Bmp5 sgRNA combinations varied significantly: injecting sgRNAs 2,3 led to fewer ampullary organs in 78% of cases (n=28/36) versus 39% for sgRNAs 1,2,3 (n=16/41) and 23% for sgRNAs 1,4 (n=9/39).
claims.source: The efficacy of different sgRNA combinations varied significantly: injecting sgRNAs 2,3 led to fewer ampullary organs in 78% of cases (n=28/36; Supplementary file 1) versus 39% for sgRNAs 1,2,3 (n=16/41) and 23% for sgRNAs 1,4 (n=9/39; Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by counting data in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Of the 43 genotyped Bmp5 crispants, 33 had a positive 'knock-out' score, confirming successful disruption of the targeted gene.
claims.source: Of the 43 genotyped crispants, 33 had a positive 'knock-out' score, confirming successful disruption of the targeted gene (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by genotyping data in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: The genotyping primers for Bmp5 only amplify the chromosome 6 ohnolog, owing to mismatches with the chromosome 5 ohnolog.
claims.source: Our genotyping primers were designed before chromosome-level sterlet genomes were available; comparison with the reference genome (NCBI RefSeq assembly GCF_902713425.1) showed that only the chromosome 6 ohnolog can be amplified, owing to mismatches with the chromosome 5 ohnolog (primarily because the reverse primer targeted an intron).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by analysis of the sterlet reference genome.

claims.claim: The ICE knock-out score was zero for ten Bmp5 crispants that nevertheless displayed the phenotype of reduced number of ampullary organs, which may be explained by the genotyping primers only amplifying the chromosome 6 ohnolog, combined with crispant mosaicism.
claims.source: This, combined with crispant mosaicism, may explain why the ICE knock-out score was zero for ten Bmp5 crispants that nevertheless displayed the phenotype of reduced number of ampullary organs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the genotyping data and the limitations of the genotyping approach.

claims.claim: ISH for the electroreceptor-specific marker Kcnab3 confirmed the reduction in ampullary organ number in Bmp5 crispants relative to control Tyr crispants.
claims.source: To examine the disruption in ampullary organ formation further, 15 control Tyr crispants and 13 Bmp5 crispants (six injected with sgRNAs 2,3 and seven injected with sgRNAs 1,4; Supplementary file 1) were subjected to ISH for the electroreceptor-specific marker Kcnab3 (Modrell et al., 2017a; Minařík et al., 2024a). Relative to control Tyr crispants (Figure 4G–I), this confirmed the reduction in ampullary organ number when there was no possibility of confusing the two sensory organ types (Figure 4J–L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4G-L.

claims.claim: Post-ISH Sox2 immunostaining revealed no obvious phenotype in the number and morphology of neuromasts in Bmp5 crispants.
claims.source: The same Bmp5 crispants were then immunostained post-ISH for the supporting cell marker Sox2 (Hernández et al., 2007; Modrell et al., 2017a), which labels neuromasts more strongly than ampullary organs (Modrell et al., 2017a; Minařík et al., 2024a) and revealed no obvious phenotype in the number and morphology of neuromasts (Figure 4J1, K1 and L1; compare with Figure 4J, K and L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4J1, K1 and L1.

claims.claim: Very few 'additional' ampullary organs appeared after Sox2 immunostaining in Bmp5 crispants, suggesting that disrupting the Bmp5 gene prevented ampullary organ formation, rather than blocking the later differentiation of Kcnab3-positive electroreceptors within ampullary organs.
claims.source: Furthermore, very few 'additional' ampullary organs appeared after Sox2 immunostaining (Figure 4J1,K1 and L1; compare with Figure 4J, K and L), suggesting that disrupting the Bmp5 gene prevented ampullary organ formation, rather than blocking the later differentiation of Kcnab3-positive electroreceptors within ampullary organs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4J1, K1 and L1.

claims.claim: Bmp5 crispants had significantly fewer ampullary organs overall than Tyr control crispants (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Statistical analysis using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank sum) test revealed that Bmp5 crispants had significantly fewer ampullary organs overall than Tyr control crispants (p<0.0001; Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 5A and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: All ampullary organ fields except for the dorsal supraorbital field had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants.
claims.source: Indeed, all ampullary organ fields except for the dorsal supraorbital field (one of the smaller fields) had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: The dorsal supraorbital field originates from the anterodorsal lateral line placode.
claims.source: The dorsal supraorbital field originates from the anterodorsal lateral line placode, which also gives rise to the ventral supraorbital and the dorsal and ventral infraorbital fields, all of which had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants (p=0.0008, p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively; two-tailed Mann-Whitney test; Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature (Gibbs and Northcutt, 2004).

claims.claim: The anterodorsal lateral line placode also gives rise to the ventral supraorbital and the dorsal and ventral infraorbital fields.
claims.source: The dorsal supraorbital field originates from the anterodorsal lateral line placode, which also gives rise to the ventral supraorbital and the dorsal and ventral infraorbital fields, all of which had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants (p=0.0008, p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively; two-tailed Mann-Whitney test; Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature (Gibbs and Northcutt, 2004).

claims.claim: The ventral supraorbital, dorsal infraorbital, and ventral infraorbital fields all had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants (p=0.0008, p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively).
claims.source: The dorsal supraorbital field originates from the anterodorsal lateral line placode, which also gives rise to the ventral supraorbital and the dorsal and ventral infraorbital fields, all of which had significantly fewer ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants versus control Tyr crispants (p=0.0008, p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively; two-tailed Mann-Whitney test; Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: The lack of effect in the dorsal supraorbital field may simply reflect the relatively small number of ampullary organs.
claims.source: Thus, the lack of effect in the dorsal supraorbital field may simply reflect the relatively small number of ampullary organs (although this is not the smallest field).
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the reason for the lack of a significant effect in the dorsal supraorbital field.

claims.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeting of Bmp5 in G0-injected embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs developing in almost all fields.
claims.source: Overall, these data show that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeting of Bmp5 in G0-injected embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs developing in almost all fields.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the CRISPR/Cas9 data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: Bmp5, which is expressed in ampullary organ primordia as well as in mature ampullary organs, normally acts to promote ampullary organ formation.
claims.source: This suggests that Bmp5, which is expressed in ampullary organ primordia as well as in mature ampullary organs (Figure 1), normally acts to promote ampullary organ formation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the CRISPR/Cas9 data and the Bmp5 expression data.

claims.claim: Stage 36 (newly hatched) sterlet yolk-sac larvae were treated with DMH1 for 20 hours, by which point (at 16 °C) they will have reached approximately stage 38.
claims.source: We treated stage 36 (newly hatched) sterlet yolk-sac larvae with DMH1 for 20 hours, by which point (at 16 °C) they will have reached approximately stage 38: that is, just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development (ISH for Eya4 showed that ampullary organ primordia are present in all the main fields by stage 39; Minařík et al., 2024a).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claims.claim: Stage 38 is just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development.
claims.source: We treated stage 36 (newly hatched) sterlet yolk-sac larvae with DMH1 for 20 hours, by which point (at 16 °C) they will have reached approximately stage 38: that is, just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development (ISH for Eya4 showed that ampullary organ primordia are present in all the main fields by stage 39; Minařík et al., 2024a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: ISH for Eya4 showed that ampullary organ primordia are present in all the main fields by stage 39.
claims.source: We treated stage 36 (newly hatched) sterlet yolk-sac larvae with DMH1 for 20 hours, by which point (at 16 °C) they will have reached approximately stage 38: that is, just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development (ISH for Eya4 showed that ampullary organ primordia are present in all the main fields by stage 39; Minařík et al., 2024a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication by the authors.

claims.claim: In comparison to DMSO controls (n=12), more ampullary organs had formed by stage 45 in all DMH1-treated larvae (n=17/17).
claims.source: In comparison to DMSO controls (n=12), more ampullary organs had formed by stage 45 in all DMH1-treated larvae (n=17/17), as visualised by ISH for the hair cell/electroreceptor marker Cacna1d (Figure 6A–D; n=8) or for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 (Figure 6E–H; n=9).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6A-H.

claims.claim: The increase in ampullary organ number in DMH1-treated larvae was most striking in the dorsalmost ampullary organ fields, i.e., the dorsal supraorbital, dorsal otic and supratemporal fields.
claims.source: The increase in ampullary organ number seemed to be general but was most striking in the dorsalmost ampullary organ fields, i.e., the dorsal supraorbital, dorsal otic and supratemporal fields.
claims.evidence: This is an observation based on the in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: In DMH1-treated larvae, there were so many ampullary organs in the dorsalmost fields that the fields appeared to fuse together in a line.
claims.source: These fields were clearly separate in the DMSO control larvae (Figure 6A, B, E and F). However, in the DMH1-treated larvae, there were so many ampullary organs that the fields appeared to fuse together in a line (Figure 6C, D, G and H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6C, D, G and H.

claims.claim: ISH for Cacna1d showed that the three dorsal ampullary organ fields were still clearly separate even in much older larvae.
claims.source: ISH for Cacna1d showed that the three dorsal ampullary organ fields were still clearly separate even in much older larvae (Figure 6I and J), suggesting that the supernumerary ampullary organs in this region of DMH1-treated larvae at stage 45 were ectopic, rather than precocious.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6I and J.

claims.claim: The supernumerary ampullary organs in the dorsalmost region of DMH1-treated larvae at stage 45 were ectopic, rather than precocious.
claims.source: ISH for Cacna1d showed that the three dorsal ampullary organ fields were still clearly separate even in much older larvae (Figure 6I and J), suggesting that the supernumerary ampullary organs in this region of DMH1-treated larvae at stage 45 were ectopic, rather than precocious.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6I and J.

claims.claim: The Cacna1d expression pattern in several DMH1-treated larvae suggested the presence of ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line (n=5/8).
claims.source: Although the increased number of ampullary organs in the dorsal fields was the most obvious and consistent phenotype, the Cacna1d expression pattern in several larvae suggested the presence of ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line (Figure 6K and L; n=5/8).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6K and L.

claims.claim: ISH for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 followed by immunostaining for Sox2 showed that the ectopic organs were indeed neuromasts (n=5/6).
claims.source: We therefore took six of the nine larvae that had been subjected to ISH for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 and immunostained them for the supporting cell marker Sox2, which labels neuromasts more strongly than ampullary organs (also see Minařík et al., 2024a). This enabled direct comparison of the same larvae with and without visible neuromasts and showed that the ectopic organs were indeed neuromasts (Figure 6M-N1; n=5/6 as in one larva it was not clear whether an ectopic offshoot was indeed present).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6M-N1.

claims.claim: Ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line were seen in a majority of larvae (n=10/14; 71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36.
claims.source: Overall, therefore, ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line (compare Figure 6M1,N1 with wildtype Sox2 expression at stage 45 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K and L) were seen in a majority of larvae (n=10/14; 71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36, where this could be determined (n=5/8 after ISH for Cacna1d; n=5/6 after ISH for Kcnab3 followed by immunostaining for Sox2).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the data on ectopic neuromast offshoots.

claims.claim: At stage 36, neuromast primordia are already forming in the supraorbital primordium.
claims.source: At stage 36, neuromast primordia are already forming in the supraorbital primordium (as shown by Sox2 expression; Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claims.claim: At stages 36–38, immunoreactivity for pSMAD1/5/9 suggests that Bmp signalling is most prominent in lateral line nerves, rather than the supraorbital lateral line primordium.
claims.source: At stages 36–38, immunoreactivity for pSMAD1/5/9 suggests that Bmp signalling is most prominent in this region in lateral line nerves, rather than the supraorbital lateral line primordium (Figure 2E–H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E-H.

claims.claim: The Bmp signalling activity during stages 36–38 that is required to prevent ectopic secondary neuromast formation from the supraorbital neuromast line might be active in lateral line nerves, rather than the lateral line primordium itself.
claims.source: This suggests the intriguing hypothesis that the Bmp signalling activity during stages 36–38 (the approximate period of DMH1 treatment) that is required to prevent ectopic secondary neuromast formation from the supraorbital neuromast line, might be active in lateral line nerves, rather than the lateral line primordium itself.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the immunohistochemistry data and the DMH1 treatment results.

claims.claim: DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Statistical analysis using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank sum) test confirmed that DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001; Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 7A and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: All individual ampullary organ fields had significantly more ampullary organs in DMH1-treated larvae than in DMSO controls.
claims.source: This was also the case for each individual ampullary organ field (Figure 7B; Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 7B and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: DMH1-treated larvae (n=17) had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae (n=10), both overall (p<0.0001) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields.
claims.source: Furthermore, the DMH1-treated larvae (n=17) had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae (n=10), both overall (p<0.0001; Figure 8A) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields (Figure 8B; Supplementary file 3; the same colour-coded schematic is shown in Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 8A and B and Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: There was no significant difference between ampullary organ numbers in 2.0 cm versus 2.8 cm wild-type larvae, either overall (p=0.4206) or in any individual field (p>0.05 for each field).
claims.source: (Note: the five 2.0 cm and five 2.8 cm wild-type larvae were grouped together for statistical comparison with DMH1-treated larvae because using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney test showed that there was no significant difference between ampullary organ numbers in 2.0 cm versus 2.8 cm larvae, either overall [p=0.4206] or in any individual field [p>0.05 for each field].)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data in Supplementary file 3.

claims.claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36, before the first ampullary organ primordia form, results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
claims.source: Overall, these results show that blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36, before the first ampullary organ primordia form, results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claims.claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36 results in ectopic ampullary organs forming in the dorsalmost fields.
claims.source: Furthermore, ectopic ampullary organs form in the dorsalmost fields, and an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line develops in a majority of larvae.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claims.claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36 results in an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line developing in a majority of larvae.
claims.source: Furthermore, ectopic ampullary organs form in the dorsalmost fields, and an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line develops in a majority of larvae.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claims.claim: During normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
claims.source: This suggests that during normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the DMH1 treatment data.

claims.claim: Bmp5 proved to be expressed in ampullary organ primordia (though not neuromast primordia), as well as in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet.
claims.source: In this study, we identified opposing roles for Bmp signalling in ampullary organ development in sterlet. We began by investigating Bmp5, the only Bmp ligand gene in our late-larval paddlefish lateral line organ-enriched gene-set (Modrell et al., 2017a). In sterlet, Bmp5 proved to be expressed in ampullary organ primordia (though not neuromast primordia), as well as in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the Bmp5 expression data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Significantly fewer ampullary organs formed when Bmp5 was targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos.
claims.source: Significantly fewer ampullary organs formed when Bmp5 was targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos, suggesting that during normal development, Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ formation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the CRISPR/Cas9 data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: Blocking Bmp signalling globally at stages just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development led to significantly more ampullary organs forming in all fields.
claims.source: In contrast, blocking Bmp signalling globally at stages just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development led to significantly more ampullary organs forming in all fields.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claims.claim: Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
claims.source: Hence, Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the DMH1 treatment data.

claims.claim: The precise function and timing of action of Bmp5 in promoting ampullary organ formation remain to be determined.
claims.source: The early expression of Bmp5 in ampullary organ primordia, but not neuromast primordia, suggested a role specifically in ampullary organ development. Indeed, targeting Bmp5 for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs forming, with no effect on neuromast formation. Its precise function and timing of action in promoting ampullary organ formation remain to be determined.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study and future directions.

claims.claim: It could be informative to test whether inhibiting Bmp signalling using DMH1 for discrete periods at successively later time-points recapitulates the Bmp5 crispant phenotype.
claims.source: Although beyond the scope of this study, it could be informative to test whether inhibiting Bmp signalling using DMH1 for discrete periods at successively later time-points recapitulates the Bmp5 crispant phenotype.
